actions: Continue the 20% peak café capacity reservation pilot in 50 US cafés through February 2027, maintaining the cap on mobile pickup slots and up to two additional peak staff-hours per weekday per store.

Collect and analyze instrumentation data on order attempts, slot offers, completions, refunds, staffing, and baseline-linked repeat purchases for both pilot and comparison cafés. Do not expand beyond the 50-store pilot or change beverage pricing.
moves.rationale: Starbucks’ core incentive is to defend in-café experience and transaction growth without sacrificing digital convenience or channel contribution. The current pilot is consistent with operational capabilities and resource constraints, and allows for reversible, evidence-based learning. Continuing the pilot with robust measurement is necessary to meet the internal decision rules for wait reduction and contribution before any further escalation or rollback. No additional moves (e.g., price changes, broader rollout, or increased staffing) are justified without passing the required evidence gates.
resource_commitments: Maintain up to two additional peak staff-hours per weekday per pilot store (totaling up to $60/store/day at $30/hour).
Instrument and monitor all relevant order and staffing data in the 50 pilot and 50 comparison cafés.
No changes to beverage pricing or expansion beyond the pilot scope.
expected_responses: Dutch Bros and Dunkin are likely to sustain or modestly intensify their localized promotions and labor investments to capture mobile and value-seeking customers displaced by Starbucks’ capped mobile slots.

Some mobile-first or time-sensitive customers will continue to shift to competitors or home preparation if mobile slots are unavailable, while walk-in customers will benefit from improved in-café service.
Competitors may monitor Starbucks’ pilot for signs of repeat loss or operational strain but are unlikely to make major new moves unless Starbucks expands or changes terms.
